speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) what are the criteria that NParks uses to make decisions about tree cutting and/or replanting activities in residential estates; (b) whether these criteria vary according to the location and nature of the residential estate and, if so, how; and (c) how are residents consulted in the process.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: In doing so, NParks considers factors like the site condition and landscaping scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For example, where space is limited or tight, a small or medium-sized tree will be chosen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: NParks is committed to conserving the trees under its care as much as possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Our green spaces and trees are precious and NParks does its best to ensure that Singaporeans can enjoy them well into the future.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In cases where a tree is replaced because it is in ill health or for some other reason, in some cases, I believe that a different species of tree is planted from the species that was planted before.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I just wish to know what are the considerations behind that.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Are there biodiversity considerations, or aesthetic or residents' feedback considerations?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And where species switch is made in the replacement, is there some consultation aspect?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Just as context, I received this feedback from a resident in East Coast, who noticed there was some change in the species mix of trees in the area, and that is why I am asking the question.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In the Member's example, it is to replace a tree that had to be felled because it was ill and cannot be saved.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Of course, we look at considerations, such as the ability to provide shade, screening for privacy, and the ability to survive urban environment stresses and ease of maintenance.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Can I ask the Senior Minister of State if the guidelines for NParks are identical to those for HDB?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: In HDB estates, especially in older car parks in mature estates, I am sure residents and Singaporeans appreciate the foliage and the cover that the trees provide, but a big problem is some of the roots of the trees will start to protrude between car park slabs, causing accidents and things of that nature.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Under what circumstances would a Town Council be allowed, with HDB's permission, to replace that tree with one whose growth can be controlled in the long term, with the roots perhaps not spreading out so much, particularly for mature estates?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, if the Town Councils' horticulturists have concerns, please flag out to HDB and ask them to consult NParks if you feel that there is a need to delve a bit deeper into the types of trees that need to be replanted.
